title: City of Waterloo asks for community assistance in return of missing public artwork
body:
The City of Waterloo is asking for the return of a public artwork that was located in front of the King Street parkade.
Triad: Dual, Interface and Reunited
, by artist Ann Roberts, was the first public art piece to be commissioned by the City of Waterloo in 1981. It was reported missing October 29, 2026.
Public art contributes to the character, identity and vibrancy of our community. It is intended to be enjoyed by everyone, and its theft represents a loss not only of the artwork itself, but of a shared community asset.
“The Roberts family is deeply saddened by the theft of Triad: Dual, Interface and Reunited,” the family shared with the City. “Our mother, Ann Roberts, has been a longtime and passionate supporter of the arts in Waterloo, caring deeply about the community and its cultural life. We are hopeful that the work will be found and returned so that it can once again be enjoyed by the community.”
The three bronze sculptures that make up
Triad: Dual, Interface and Reunited
were cast by the lost wax method. There are references to bones, armour and helmets in the work. However, by suggesting human or vegetative qualities, the artist introduces hope and regeneration into the detritus of harsh and menacing war time conflicts.
“Theft of public artwork is particularly disappointing because these pieces belong to the entire community,” said Sonya Poweska, culture program specialist at the City of Waterloo. “Public art helps make our public spaces welcoming, engaging and unique. We hope the artwork can be recovered and returned to the community.”
The City is working with Waterloo Regional Police Service to investigate the incident. Anyone with information about the theft or the whereabouts of the artwork is asked to call police at 519-570-9777, extension 6399.
The City of Waterloo and the Roberts family appreciate the community's assistance in returning this important piece of the City’s public art collection.
